Hypotrochoids

Spirograph-like curves arise from simple sums of rotating vectors; a tiny tweak in frequency or phase yields striking patterns.

Compact parametric form:

$$

x(t)=R\cos t+r\cos(kt+\varphi),\\\\ y(t)=R\sin t+r\sin(kt+\varphi),

$$

where \(k\) is the frequency ratio. Rational \(k\) ⇒ closed patterns; irrational \(k\) ⇒ long, nonrepeating traces. ℂ numbers allow to write such expressions much shorter, for instance:

ParametricPlot[ReIm[(*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)-t](*]SpB*) + 3 (*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)t/3](*]SpB*)], {t, 0, 4Pi}] We can nicely decompose it back into 2 components and animate it using `Animate` expression and bunch of arrows:

Animate[ ParametricPlot[ReIm[(*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)-t](*]SpB*) + 3 (*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)t/3](*]SpB*)], {t,0,u}, Epilog->{ Arrow[{{0,0}, ReIm[(*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)-u](*]SpB*)]}], Arrow[{ ReIm[(*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)-u](*]SpB*)], ReIm[(*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)-u](*]SpB*) + 3 (*SpB[*)Power[I(*|*),(*|*)u/3](*]SpB*)]}] }, PlotRange->{{-4,4}, {-4,4}}, GridLines->Automatic, PlotStyle->(*VB[*)(RGBColor[1, 0, 0])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNiYGAo5gUSYZmp5S6pyflFiSX5RcEsQBHn4PCQNGaQPAeQCHJ3cs7PyS8qYgCDD/ZQBgMDnAEA4iUPRg=="*)(*]VB*) ] , {u, 0.001, 4Pi}, RefreshRate->30, Appearance->None] :::note

Here we start from `0.001` to avoid zeros in `ParametricPlot`, othwersize it will throw a warning message

:::
